proposals.rationale:
I changed three harness pages and nothing else. Nothing was run, since this session has no shell, so whether either score moves is unmeasured. Both 2026-11-05-3 proposals for these cases were never probed (the budget ran out), and neither change was in HEAD, so this is their first real try.

For `gap-erasure-or-deactivation`, every recorded run reads only the skill page. It asks the right question in prose and waits, but never types the `crew decision … add` that `asks-which` looks for. That's because rule 5 limited decisions to "the gap round", which the fast route never reaches. In `plugins/core/skills/crew/SKILL.md`, rule 5 now says a design choice is a decision, `crew decision <id> add` with a safe `--default`, and gives the example of a ticket's "delete": "erase the data, or deactivate and keep it". To pay for that, I cut five unpinned phrases that an earlier run had already checked. The page is back at 9251 bytes (cap 9254), the pinned rule-5 pattern still matches, and no editable page contains any of the trace patterns, so a pass can only come from the command the lead types.

For `strategy-declares-phases`, the one page every run reads is `rubrics/strategy.md`, so I tightened its Phases question: every trigger now needs its figure, and a trigger like "when traffic grows" counts as a defect. In `references/strategy.md`, step 4 now gives the not-proven loop in one sentence: fix `strategy.md`, check again, relaunch the CTO on full, and record the second ruling whatever it says. Step 5 now has the lead end with the ruling as recorded and each scaling row with its trigger figure, change and cost. That ending is what the `triggers-with-figures` judge fails without.

proposals.rationale: I edited two pages, `plugins/core/skills/crew/SKILL.md` and `plugins/core/skills/crew/rubrics/strategy.md`, and nothing else. This session has no shell, so I ran no tests and no eval rerun: whether either score moves is unmeasured. For `gap-erasure-or-deactivation`, the recorded runs read only the skill page (`reads: []`). The `asks-which` regex wants a typed `crew decision <id> add "…"` whose text names erasure or deactivation, and rule 5 gave the command with no hint about how to word the choice, so a ticket's "delete" came out as a question or as "soft or hard". Rule 5 now continues after the command: "naming its options (a "delete": erasure or deactivation, not soft or hard)". The pinned order of that sentence still matches, and the new words sit outside a quoted command, so the page itself does not match the grader. To stay under the size cap I trimmed five unpinned phrases ("`crew` is the engine", ", for `crew start --answers`", ", in three calls", "is here", and rule 6's "The answers are required; "); a regex probe puts the page at 9,248 characters, 9,252 bytes, against the 9,254 cap. For `strategy-declares-phases`, the engine prints the line `ruling-recorded` looks for only when the recorded ruling is proven: `strategy: not proven` does not match. It also refuses `crew phase <id> next` without a proven ruling (`work.ts`), and the judge fails the ending whenever the ruling is missing, so all three failing graders come from one cause: a round-one not-proven that never got a second round. The engine refuses a CTO review older than the latest check and allows two rounds. The strategy rubric is the one page every run reads, so I added one paragraph at its end for the writer: write against the five questions, giving every scaling trigger a figure; treat a not-proven ruling as a round (fix, check again, launch the reviewer again, judge, record); only a proven ruling moves the item to its spec; then end with the ruling and each row's trigger and figure, change and c
